newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee falls on dlr demand from east India.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee falls on dlr demand from east India.

text.p: The Indian rupee fell to 35.95 per dollar in noon trade on Monday on heavy demand from a large state-run bank based in eastern India, dealers said.
"The state-run bank hit the market in a pretty big way in late morning," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
He said the bank began buying at 35.87.
"The market was taken a bit by surprise. Some banks appear to have been caught short..this added to the demand," the dealer said.
Dealers said they did not expect the rupee to fall any further. "It should hold around 35.95 for the present," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
The dollar was quoted 35.93/95 rupees in latest deals.
